target: Fate silenzio durante la presentazione.
english: Be quiet during the presentation.
tip: The voi command is simply the present voi form: fare gives fate, so fate silenzio means (you all) be quiet.

target: Vada dritto fino al semaforo.
english: Go straight to the traffic light.
tip: Formal commands to someone you address as Lei use the subjunctive: andare gives vada (go, formal).

target: Portategli un regalo per il compleanno.
english: Bring him a birthday present.
tip: Gli means to him as an indirect object, and here it attaches to the command: portate + gli = portategli.

target: Vorrei un caffè macchiato, per favore.
english: I'd like a macchiato, please.
tip: Vorrei is the conditional of volere and is the polite way to order or ask: Vorrei un caffe means I'd like a coffee.

target: I prezzi aumenteranno il prossimo mese.
english: Prices will increase next month.
tip: The loro (they) future ends in -anno: aumentare gives aumenteranno (they will increase).

target: Finite i compiti prima di uscire.
english: Finish your homework before going out.
tip: Prima di takes the infinitive to mean before doing something: prima di uscire means before going out.

target: Non vi arrabbiate per così poco.
english: Don't get angry over so little.
tip: A negative voi command keeps the normal voi form after non: non vi arrabbiate means don't (you all) get angry.

target: Non dire bugie, si scopre sempre.
english: Don't tell lies, it always comes out.
tip: Impersonal si plus a verb means one or it, with no named subject: si scopre means it gets found out.

target: Mettici più impegno la prossima volta.
english: Put more effort into it next time.
tip: Ci can mean into it or on it and attaches to the command: metti + ci = mettici, put more into it.

target: Berrò solo acqua durante la dieta.
english: I'll drink only water during the diet.
tip: Bere has an irregular future built on the stem berr-: berrò means I will drink, not the expected bevrò.

target: Sbrigatevi, il film sta per iniziare!
english: Hurry up, the movie is about to start!
tip: Stare per plus the infinitive means to be about to do something: sta per iniziare means it's about to start.

target: Costerà molto quel ristorante, non credi?
english: That restaurant will cost a lot, don't you think?
tip: The future tense can express a guess about the present: costerà molto means it probably costs a lot.

target: Avresti tempo di accompagnarmi alla stazione?
english: Would you have time to take me to the station?
tip: Avresti is the conditional of avere and softens a request: Avresti tempo means would you have time.

target: Cercherò un volo economico per le vacanze.
english: I'll look for a cheap flight for the vacation.
tip: Verbs in -care add an h in the future to keep the hard c sound: cercare gives cercherò (I will look for).

target: Mangerai con noi o hai già cenato?
english: Will you eat with us or have you already had dinner?
tip: Verbs in -giare drop the i in the future: mangiare gives mangerai (you will eat), not mangierai.

target: La cena sarà servita alle otto in punto.
english: Dinner will be served at eight o'clock sharp.
tip: The passive uses essere plus the past participle, which agrees with the subject: sarà servita (fem) means will be served.

target: A che ora dovremmo partire per arrivare puntuali?
english: What time should we leave to arrive on time?
tip: Dovremmo is the conditional of dovere and means should, for suggestions: dovremmo partire means we should leave.

target: Quando avrò risparmiato abbastanza, comprerò una macchina nuova.
english: When I've saved enough, I'll buy a new car.
tip: The future perfect, avrò plus the participle, marks what finishes first: avrò risparmiato means once I've saved.

target: Avevamo camminato per ore prima di trovare l'hotel.
english: We had walked for hours before finding the hotel.
tip: The trapassato (imperfect of avere or essere plus participle) marks an earlier past: avevamo camminato means we had walked.

target: Mi chiedevo se potrebbe aiutarmi con una cosa.
english: I was wondering if you could help me with something.
tip: Conditional potere is the polite 'could': potrebbe aiutarmi means 'could you help me', the go-to softener with strangers.

target: Dopo una giornata così, mi farei un bel bagno caldo.
english: After a day like this, I'd take a nice hot bath.
tip: Farsi means to do something for yourself: mi farei un bagno is 'I'd run myself a bath', a reflexive where English has none.

target: Non parlare con la bocca piena!
english: Don't talk with your mouth full!
tip: To forbid, Italian switches to the infinitive: parla means 'speak', but Non parlare means 'don't speak'.

target: Non dirgli niente, è una sorpresa.
english: Don't tell him anything, it's a surprise.
tip: The negative tu command uses the infinitive with the pronoun glued on: Non dirgli means 'don't tell him'.

target: Mi piacerebbe imparare a suonare il piano.
english: I'd like to learn to play the piano.
tip: Mi piacerebbe is literally 'it would please me': the thing liked is the subject, and the wanter is mi.

target: Sicuramente, accetterei quell'offerta di lavoro.
english: I'd definitely accept that job offer.
tip: Quella drops to quell' before a feminine word starting with a vowel: quell'offerta, not quella offerta.

target: Saranno partiti senza di noi.
english: They must have left without us.
tip: Senza adds di before a pronoun: senza di noi, senza di me. Before a noun it stands alone: senza zucchero.

target: Quando avrò tempo, ti chiamerò.
english: When I have time, I'll call you.
tip: After quando Italian keeps the future: Quando avrò tempo is literally 'when I will have time', where English uses the present.

target: Avrà trent'anni, più o meno.
english: He must be about thirty years old.
tip: Future of probability: avrà = 'he probably has'.

target: Quando arriverai, sarò già partito.
english: When you arrive, I'll have already left.
tip: The future perfect of a motion verb uses essere: sarò partito means 'I'll have left', never avrò.

target: Saranno usciti senza dirci niente.
english: They must have gone out without telling us.
tip: After senza, Italian uses the infinitive, not the -ing form: senza dirci niente = without telling us anything.
